lineage_context.teaching_goal: Show how the mustard sister lineage keeps a 4-petal plan but diverges toward glandular compound leaves, asymmetric flowers, numerous exserted stamens and elongated capsules.

project_scope.selection_mode: Clammyweed-centered project module with current-name reconciliation
project_scope.note: The Master Pool uses Polanisia names from older/FNA sources. Current Kew accepts Cleome dodecandra and treats Polanisia dodecandra as a synonym; the old P. dodecandra subsp. trachysperma concept maps to accepted Cleome trachysperma.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: For the local clammyweed pattern, look for a sticky/glandular herb with palmately 3-foliolate leaves, a 4-petal somewhat asymmetric flower, many long exserted stamens, and a long 2-valved capsule.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Annual or perennial herbs to shrubs; leaves often palmately compound, commonly 3 or more leaflets; glandular hairs are common in the local clammyweed pattern.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually 4-sepaled and 4-petaled, often more asymmetric than Brassicaceae. Stamens commonly 6 to many; local dodecandra/trachysperma concepts have roughly 10–20 long exserted stamens.
family_diagnostics.fruit: An elongated dry capsule with two valves; the ovary/fruit may sit on a short gynophore depending on genus/species.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Sticky + 3 leaflets + four petals + a spray of long stamens is the local Cleomaceae doorway.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: glandular 3-foliolate leaf → asymmetric 4-petal flower → many exserted stamens → long capsule → modern-name card
visual_lesson.intro: Cleomaceae looks related to mustard the moment you count four petals, then immediately breaks the mustard rules with its leaves and stamens.

steps.title: 1 · Feel the architecture without touching
steps.look_for: Palmately 3-foliolate leaves and visibly glandular/sticky stems and petioles.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a fast contrast with the usually simple, exstipulate mustard leaf.

steps.title: 2 · Compare the four petals with mustard
steps.look_for: Four separate petals, but often unequal or arranged asymmetrically rather than forming a neat cross.
steps.why_it_matters: This shows the shared Brassicales blueprint and the family-level divergence.

steps.title: 3 · Count the long exserted stamens
steps.look_for: A conspicuous whiskery spray of about 10–20 long stamens in the local clammyweed concept.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest visual split from Brassicaceae's 6-stamen 4-long/2-short pattern.

steps.title: 4 · Follow the ovary to the capsule
steps.look_for: An elongated dry 2-valved capsule, often conspicuously longer than the flower.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit confirms the family while preserving the visible relationship to mustard-like dry fruits.

steps.title: 5 · Learn the current-name update
steps.look_for: Polanisia dodecandra → Cleome dodecandra; Polanisia dodecandra subsp. trachysperma → Cleome trachysperma in current Kew treatment.
steps.why_it_matters: Lets you read older Central Texas floras without creating duplicate learner taxa.

comparisons.title: Cleomaceae vs Brassicaceae
comparisons.rule: Cleomaceae local pattern: glandular/sticky, palmately 3-foliolate, more asymmetric 4-petal flower, 10–20 exserted stamens. Brassicaceae: usually simple alternate leaves, regular cross-shaped flower, 6 tetradynamous stamens and replum-bearing silique/silicle.

comparisons.title: Cleomaceae vs Fabaceae
comparisons.rule: Three leaflets can suggest legumes, but Cleomaceae flowers have four petals and many exposed stamens, and the capsule is not a one-carpel legume.

visual_lesson.caveat: Cleomaceae is broader than the local Polanisia/Cleome pattern. Do not make three leaflets or 10–20 stamens universal across the entire family.

genera.fast_cue: glandular 3-foliolate herb + 4 unequal petals + many exserted stamens + long capsule
